previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fever, right flank pain, and cloudy urine, concerning for pyelonephritis and urosepsis, eight days after discharge from a prior admission for ileal conduit urinary diversion. He had leukocytosis, acute kidney injury, and imaging showed bilateral hydronephrosis. Urine cultures grew Enterococcus species, including VRE, prompting addition of daptomycin to meropenem. He initially refused some antibiotic doses, but psychiatry confirmed he had capacity to make that decision. His infection resolved, with improvement in white count and renal function. A PICC line was placed for outpatient IV antibiotics. He was discharged home with visiting nurse services to complete a 12-day course of meropenem and 7-day course of daptomycin, along with instructions for low-potassium diet and close follow-up.

Dear Mr. ___,

of your kidney function. 

You were found to have an obstruction of your left ureter. The 
Interventional Radiologists initially placed a tube out of your

make good urine. You will have follow up appointments with your 
Urologist and Interventional Radiologist to exchange this stent 
(see below).

You were also were given strong IV antibiotics to treat your 
urinary and kidney infection. 

Please make sure you have your labs checked when you see your 
PCP to monitor both your white blood cells and kidney function.

It you have any worsening abdominal pain, fevers, chills or any 
other concerning symptom, please seek medical attention.

Again, it was our pleasure participating in your care.

We wish you the ___,

INDICATION:  ___ year old man s/p ileal conduit ___ here w/ pyelo and AoCKD
(Cr 7 from 3s), s/p loopogram showing likely left ureteral obstruction. Please
obtain an anterior nephrostogram. If truly obstructed, if stricture and
amenable, please place PCNU. Otherwise he will need left PCN // please perform

ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
200 mcg of fentanyl and 4 mg of midazolam throughout the total intra-service
time of 45 min during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse. 1% lidocaine
was injected in the skin and subcutaneous tissues overlying the access site.

MEDICATIONS: Meropenem, fentanyl, midazolam, lidocaine

CONTRAST: 40 ml of Optiray contrast.

FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE: 9 min, 7 mGy

PROCEDURE:  1. Left ultrasound guided renal collecting system access.
2. Left nephrostogram.
3. Left 8 ___ nephrostomy tube placement.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient. The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed
supine on the exam table. A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___
protocol. The left flank was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.

After the injection of 5 cc of 1% lidocaine in the subcutaneous soft tissues,
the right renal collecting system was accessed through a posterior lower pole
calyx under ultrasound guidance using a 21 gauge Cook needle. Ultrasound
images of the access were stored on PACS. Prompt return of urine confirmed
appropriate positioning. Injection of a small amount of contrast outlined a
dilated renal collecting system. Under fluoroscopic guidance, a Nitinol wire
was advanced into the renal collecting system. After a skin ___, the needle
was exchanged for an Accustick sheath. One the tip of the sheath was in the
collecting system; the sheath was advanced over the wire, inner dilator and
metallic stiffener. The wire and inner dilator were then removed and diluted
contrast was injected into the collecting system to confirm position. A
glidewire was advanced through the sheath but could not be advanced through
the ureteropelvic junction. The glidewire was exchanged for an Amplatz wire
was advanced through the sheath and coiled in the collecting system.  At this
time, the decision was made to place a park nephrostomy to decompress this
system.

The sheath was then removed and a 8 ___ nephrostomy tube was advanced into
the renal collecting system. The wire was then removed and the pigtail was
formed in the collecting system. Contrast injection confirmed appropriate
positioning. The catheter was then flushed, 0 silk stay sutures applied and
the catheter was secured with a Stat Lock device and sterile dressings. The
catheter was attached to a bag.

FINDINGS: 

1. Nephrostogram demonstrating severe left-sided hydronephrosis with dilated
renal pelvis obstructing the proximal ureter.  With time minimal passage of 
contrast was noted through the tortuous proximal ureter.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful placement of 8 ___ nephrostomy on the left.  Given degree of
hydronephrosis, causing partial obstruction at the proximal ureterJ, a
percutaneous nephrostomy was placed to decompress the system. Once adequately
decompressed, we can again attempt an antegrade nephrostogram as well as need
for possible nephroureteral stent.

PROCEDURE:  1. Left nephrostogram.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient. The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed
prone on the exam table. A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___
protocol. The left flank was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.
Position of the existing nephrostomy catheter was verified by antegrade
injection of Optiray. Intrarenal position of the tip of the existing pigtail
catheter in the collecting system of the left kidney was confirmed. A
nephrostogram was performed through the existing nephrostomy catheter, and
this demonstrated a kink in the left ureter with distal ureteric narrowing.
The catheter was then cut, and ___ wire was advanced into the left renal
pelvis. The existing catheter was removed. A 6 ___ sheath was advanced over
the guidewire into the intrarenal collecting system under real-time
fluoroscopic visualization. Several attempts were made to cross the kink in
the left ureter. Using a 6 ___ 35 ___ Tip and a 5 ___ Kumpe
catheter, a Glidewire was advanced down the ureter into the ureter-ileal
anastomosis. The Glidewire was subsequently exchanged for an Amplatz wire over
